title: Show how taught words relate
statement: Introduce related new words as the structure they form, such as a web showing the concept and how the rest relate to it, not as a deck of equal cards.
example: One review cut a 6-card deck whose words formed one concept, three words for a person and two for a mechanism.
detail: The review of a Grade 9 prototype dropped a deck of six tap-to-reveal word cards, since the word web already introduced the words and could show how they relate (`g9/library/text/L36b8ba.txt`, line 80). Its note argues that the six were not a list but a structure, a concept, three words describing the person and two naming the mechanism, which equal cards hide and the web shows (line 215). The review offers such notes as rationale that has not been confirmed (line 13).
against: The same note doubts the load: "Six words may also be too many for one pre-reading beat, and they are not of equal difficulty — façade and pretense are a long way harder than disloyal." (`g9/library/text/L36b8ba.txt`, line 215). The same note warns the set may be too large and uneven: "Six words may also be too many for one pre-reading beat, and they are not of equal difficulty — façade and pretense are a long way harder than disloyal." (`g9/sources/Othello_1_Feedback_DevFactory.md`, line 215).

evidence.quote: These six are not a list, they are a structure: betrayal is the concept, deceitful and untrustworthy and disloyal describe the person, and pretense and façade name the mechanism.
